name: Clear brow gel

lead: Clear brow gel is a light styling product brushed through the eyebrows to hold hairs in place. It is often used for an even, groomed look without adding color.
It is one of the lowest-cost grooming products and carries few reported risks. No research on brow gels specifically was found.

paras: A film-forming polymer, sometimes with fibers or wax, dries on the hair and fixes the brushed position.
Risks are minimal, mainly flaking, stiffness or eye irritation from product contact. The effect lasts until it is washed off.

lead: Clear brow gel is a light, usually colourless styling product brushed through the eyebrows to hold hairs in a chosen direction. Formulas typically rely on a film-forming polymer, and some add fibres or wax for texture. It is used for a groomed, uniform brow without adding colour.

Reference works describe brow gels as one of several brow cosmetics, alongside pencils, powders and shaders, used to give hairs more texture and a fuller, more defined look. No published study has examined clear brow gels specifically. [1]

paras: The gel is applied with a small wand or spoolie and brushed up and out or along the natural growth direction. It dries to a thin film that fixes the hairs. Tinted versions add colour, while clear versions leave the hair colour unchanged.

Brow shape and adornment have changed across eras: Wikipedia notes practices such as hikimayu in Japan from the 8th century, the removal of brows among high-status women in Elizabethan England, thin plucked brows in the 1920s and 1930s, and cosmetic tattooing or microblading in the 21st century. [1] Brow gels belong to the modern range of products used to add texture and definition. [1]

A polymer film coats and stiffens the hairs so they stay where they were brushed. The effect is mechanical and cosmetic and does not change hair growth, and it ends when the product is washed off. [2]
The visible effect, brows that look neater and slightly thicker, is described in reference works. [1] It has not been measured in trials.

Reported issues with such products are limited to cosmetic ones, including flaking, stiffness and eye irritation if the product contacts the eye. These come from general product experience rather than published studies on brow gels.
Clear gel is often listed as an inexpensive item that tidies brow hairs, and the site rates its effect as strong but temporary. It is commonly paired with trimming or tinting.
